title: NYC Comptroller Demands Pause of Anthropic's $2T IPO Over AI Safety
summary:
Mark Levine, who oversees more than $325B in New York City pension assets, has written to CEO Dario Amodei requesting the AI developer postpone its move to the public markets to address governance and accountability concerns. Levine, whose office has an exposure of $7M to Anthropic, demanded a specific timeline for safety audits and clearer controls before a reported $2T listing proceeds. While recent reports suggest the parties have opened discussions, Levine stated those claims are overblown, noting the only interaction has been Anthropic's confirmation of receipt of his letter.

The comptroller's demand cites a draft prospectus that devotes 80 pages to risk disclosures—nearly twice the size of its business section—and labels a White House safety accord as merely "morally binding" and insufficient. Levine pointed to warnings from within Anthropic, including an estimate of a 10% risk of human extinction within a decade and a warning that AI agent swarms could seize the internet within 6 to 12 months, potentially causing hundreds of billions in damage.

New York City Comptroller Mark Levine wrote a letter to Anthropic asking for more clarity about its safety plans and controls prior to its planned IPO: 

"Anthropic should disclose with specificity how it will implement appropriate audits and controls, the scope of what these controls are intended to address, as well as a projected timeline. This should also include an explanation of whether and how these controls will sufficiently address your call to slow the pace at which the capabilities of AI models advance."

New York City Comptroller Mark Levine is urging Anthropic to pause its planned IPO, arguing that its 'morally binding' White House AI safety accord is insufficient and citing reports that its draft prospectus devotes 80 pages to risk disclosures, nearly twice its business section.

In a letter to Dario Amodei, Levine cites his calls to slow frontier AI and demands audits, controls, stronger governance and a timeline before a reported $2 trillion listing. He also cites Anthropic Alignment Science Lead Evan Hubinger's personal estimate of over 10% risk of AI-driven human extinction within a decade, and Amodei's warning that AI agent swarms could take over the entire internet within 6-12 months, potentially causing hundreds of billions in damage.
